We have the function 

$$
y=(5{x}^{2}+2x)^{x}.
$$

First, we take the natural logarithm of both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡((5{x}^{2}+2x)^{x}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡(5{x}^{2}+2x)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x\operatorname{ln}⁡(5{x}^{2}+2x)) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x)\cdot (\operatorname{ln}⁡(5{x}^{2}+2x))+(x)\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(5{x}^{2}+2x)) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =1\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡(5{x}^{2}+2x)+x\cdot (\frac{1}{5{x}^{2}+2x}\cdot (10x+2)) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(5{x}^{2}+2x)+\frac{10{x}^{2}+2x}{5{x}^{2}+2x}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =y(\operatorname{ln}⁡(5{x}^{2}+2x)+\frac{10{x}^{2}+2x}{5{x}^{2}+2x})\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $y=(5{x}^{2}+2x)^{x}:$    

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =(5{x}^{2}+2x)^{x}\cdot (\operatorname{ln}⁡(5{x}^{2}+2x)+\frac{10{x}^{2}+2x}{5{x}^{2}+2x}) \\  & =(5{x}^{2}+2x)^{x}\cdot (\frac{(5{x}^{2}+2x)\operatorname{ln}⁡(5{x}^{2}+2x)}{5{x}^{2}+2x}+\frac{10{x}^{2}+2x}{5{x}^{2}+2x}) \\  & =(5{x}^{2}+2x)^{x-1}\cdot ((5{x}^{2}+2x)\operatorname{ln}⁡(5{x}^{2}+2x)+10{x}^{2}+2x).\end{aligned}
$$
